testResults.name: workflow-syntax-and-expressions
testResults.result: actionlint 1.7.12 and action-validator 0.6.0 reported no workflow syntax, expression, event, permissions, or reusable-workflow schema errors

testResults.name: reusable-workflow-contract
testResults.result: workflow_call requires azure-subscription-id, resource-group, environment, and parameters-file; template-file defaults to infra/main.bicep and dry-run defaults to true

testResults.name: environment-scoped-oidc
testResults.result: The deploy job binds to inputs.environment, grants id-token: write, and azure/login receives client-id from vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID, tenant-id from vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID, and subscription-id from inputs.azure-subscription-id; no Azure client secret or secret context is used

testResults.name: resource-group-validation-and-parameter-support
testResults.result: The workflow runs az deployment group validate; .bicepparam files are passed directly, while JSON parameter files use the supplied template-file input and @path parameter syntax

testResults.name: dry-run-and-deployment-gates
testResults.result: dry-run=true runs az deployment group what-if after validation and skips deployment; dry-run=false skips what-if and runs az deployment group create after validation

testResults.name: pinned-action-revisions
testResults.command: git ls-remote against each action repository and referenced release tag
testResults.result: actions/checkout v4.2.2 and azure/login v2.3.0 are referenced by full 40-character commit SHAs

callerEnvironmentValuesRequired.purpose: Client ID of the user-assigned managed identity trusted by the environment-scoped GitHub federated credential
Microsoft Entra tenant ID containing the federated deployer identity

callerInputsRequired.purpose: Azure subscription containing the target resource group
Existing resource group to validate, preview, or deploy
Exact GitHub Environment name; it supplies the two variables above and its approval/protection rules

callerRequirements: The caller must permit id-token: write for the reusable workflow; the workflow itself requests contents: read and id-token: write.
No Azure client secret, certificate, password, or other secret is required by this workflow.
The caller must set dry-run to false explicitly to permit az deployment group create; the default is validation plus what-if only.
limitations: No Azure login, validate, what-if, deployment, or secret access was run during verification.

Verification was limited to static workflow analysis and inspection of the command paths; Azure permissions, GitHub Environment protection, and the federated credential require a GitHub-hosted caller run.
